summary: OpenAI announced that the GPT-5.6 model family (including the Sol, Terra and Luna models) is now available in AWS's Kiro coding agent, with OpenAI and AWS jointly optimizing the integration and reporting an 82% cost reduction on Terminal-Bench 2.1 tasks.

mechanisms.reason: The document states a specific cost-per-task reduction figure tied to a benchmark and describes the model as delivering more work per token at lower cost.
mechanisms.quote: Testing found that on Terminal-Bench 2.1, GPT‑5.6 Terra completed successful tasks in Kiro at roughly 82% cost reduction.

categories.reason: The announcement is specifically about OpenAI models being distributed through AWS's Kiro platform, with AWS jointly optimizing the integration.
categories.quote: OpenAI and AWS have also worked together to optimize the Kiro environment and OpenAI models.

practices.reason: A benchmark (Terminal-Bench 2.1) is cited to support a cost-reduction claim, but the test is the lab/partner's own and not independently reproducible detail.
practices.quote: Testing found that on Terminal-Bench 2.1, GPT‑5.6 Terra completed successful tasks in Kiro at roughly 82% cost reduction.

practices.reason: Kiro's spec-driven approach (structured requirements, designs, checkpoints, property-based testing) is described as a concrete technique that improves model task success and cost, which an engineering team could examine for its own agent scaffolding.
practices.quote: Kiro turns high-level intent into clear requirements, technical designs, and executable tasks.

practices.reason: The document restates that GPT-5.6 offers better performance per dollar, but gives no model-specific benchmark distinct from the Kiro integration story.
practices.quote: GPT ‑ 5.6 delivers more useful work from every token, with stronger performance per dollar and on-demand capability for complex tasks.
